title: streaming-json-resilience-oracle-with-lossy-regeneration-tests
creator: Marta Lopez
description:
Problem statement: Partial or interrupted streaming responses are a primary source of downstream consumer errors when clients expect strict JSON outputs. Existing test harnesses focus on strict pass/fail for full-stream output; they do not measure graceful recovery patterns or the practical utility of lossy regeneration strategies used by the runtime when a stream is truncated.

Goal: Build a reproducible test harness (the "Resilience Oracle") and a set of integration tests that exercise: incremental/partial-stream checkpoints, lossy-regeneration heuristics, schema-softscore tolerance thresholds, toolcall interlocks, and KV-cache aware replays. The harness should quantify functional correctness (schema adherence), consumer usability (best-effort regeneration quality), and SLO impact (latency/cost trade-offs).

Scope: This ticket covers the harness, a parametrized test matrix, and a small set of deterministic scenarios to be run against the runtime test cluster. It does not include full rollout to production canaries (follow-up ticket).

Non-goals: Rewriting the constrained decoder; benchmarking wide swaths of models. This ticket aims to validate recovery strategies and produce actionable signals for follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Resilience Oracle implemented and documented in the repository
10 parametrized scenarios that exercise different truncation points and toolcall interleavings
Automatic scoring that outputs schema-compliance percentage and a "schema-softscore" for best-effort regenerations
CI job that runs the suite on the runtime test cluster with pass/fail thresholds
Playbook entries created for when regenerations are below threshold (link included)
test_matrix_summary: Matrix axes: model size (base/medium/large), truncation position (prefix/mid/suffix), streaming rate (fast/normal/slow), KV cache state (cold/warm), toolcall interleaving (none/pre/post/in-flight), and client retry policy (none/naive/exponential). Each cell produces schema-compliance, regeneration-quality, avg latency, and token-cost metrics.
approach_notes: 1) Checkpoint tokens: insert deterministic checkpoints into streaming payloads to anchor partial replays. 2) Lossy regeneration: allow a controlled rewrite of the last N tokens using constrained-decoder with a soft schema-lint objective. 3) Scoring: compute strict JSON pass/fail and a fuzzy JSON similarity plus semantic field-level validation. 4) Toolcall handling: validate that tool invocation boundaries are preserved or corrected in regeneration. 5) KV-cache awareness: ensure replay uses appropriate cache snapshots to avoid hallucinated state.\n\nTrade-offs: Stricter regeneration reduces downstream errors but raises latency and compute; we will expose tunable knobs and measure unit economics per-test cell.
notes_and_updates: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: aligned with PM and design on tolerance bands. Marta created initial design doc.
2026-02-18 - Prototype: Ravi pushed prototype harness; initial checkpointing scheme uses a 16-token anchor sequence. Observed that warm KV-cache reduces need for aggressive regeneration.
2026-02-25 - Design review: Suggested replacing strict JSON reconciliation with a two-tier validator: strict for critical fields, soft for auxiliary fields. Design accepted.
2026-03-03 - Implementation: Added toolcall boundary detector; found edge case where toolcall mid-token caused decoder confusion. Implemented conservative boundary escape hatch.
2026-03-09 - CI: Added smoke CI job; failing on high-latency cells for large models — investigating batching vs constrained-decoder cost.
2026-03-12 - Next: Add automated scoring dashboard and flesh out playbook for below-threshold regeneration. Plan follow-up ticket to canary the end-to-end suite against dedicated pool.
